data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A single evaluation distinguishes genuine reliability gain from mere compliance by measuring whether the panel's accuracy depends on the checklist being correct; if the panel's accuracy is invariant to swapping in a deliberately degraded checklist that omits the causally relevant item, the gain is mere compliance, but if the panel's accuracy drops, the gain was genuinely checklist-dependent and the panel was using the checklist as an epistemic tool rather than a compliance ritual.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the panel's gain is from averaging independent errors rather than the checklist, the degraded checklist may not hurt, but this is a genuine gain mechanism, so the test falsely signals 'mere compliance'.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert also drops on the degraded-checklist block (because the expert also implicitly relied on the item), the test fails to separate panel and expert.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"This is a control-by-subtraction design. If the panel's performance was due to the checklist encoding the right regularities, removing the key item should hurt. If the panel was already using domain structure (genuine gain), the panel may still compensate and the drop will be smaller than expected. If the panel was merely complying, the performance should collapse or shift to whatever the degraded checklist now points to. The within-evaluation diagnostic is the performance delta between full-checklist and degraded-checklist blocks on the same panel.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
